title: First ancient DNA study (the quagga)
place: University of California, Berkeley, United States
summary: Russ Higuchi's team sequenced DNA from a museum skin of the quagga, an extinct zebra. It was the first study of what became known as ancient DNA. Within two years Svante Pääbo recovered DNA from human mummies.
why: Proved DNA can survive long after death, opening the door to ancient genomes.

notes.problem: Source says 'first study of what would come to be called aDNA', not first ancient DNA; the 1985 Egyptian-mummy date is not in the source ('over the next two years').

superlativeSource: The first study of what would come to be called aDNA was conducted in 1984
